runs.gutSentence: Yes, the weird gravity is gone and the asteroids flying about feels much more like an asteroid field. But the chasers are always right on my tail, I barely get time to set anything up. Maybe they should come in groups with some breathing room between?
themes: evaluates his own fix: the gravity feeling is gone / moving asteroids feel right
pursuers faster than him = constant pressure, little room to set traps (P1/P2)
a concrete next tweak (chaser cadence, wave pace, or wall behaviour)

runs.gutSentence: This one felt more cramped, the asteroids barely move so it's more like an obstacle course again. I liked it better when they were streaming across.
themes: asteroid motion: drifting reads as near-static / crowded compared with the streams
difficulty or density (denser field, died earlier)

runs.gutSentence: That was more like it, dodging through the streams with them smashing into rocks behind me. But most kills happen behind me where I can't see them, it doesn't feel like I'm the one doing it. Maybe something to make the luring more deliberate.
themes: reference moment 2 lands (TIE fighters in the streams)
kills happen behind/off-screen and feel accidental (P1)
proposes a next structural idea (sector variety, set pieces, or a reason to turn back toward pursuers)

runs.gutSentence: I think I prefer when the asteroids move faster in streams, these slow ones feel like they're just in the way. The flight is getting a bit samey after a while too, every sector feels the same.
themes: names the A/B difference in his own words (prefers fast/streaming rocks)
sectors feel samey / what each sector adds doesn't register
next-format idea or a request for variety in the flight

pillarForecast.why: Pursuers at 300 vs his 270 spawning every 1.3-2.4s from behind means most kills happen behind him on rocks, walls and the wave; telemetry already showed 72/83 rock kills in v5. If he notices, it's run 10's 'mostly accidental' again.
Chasers he can't outrun plus a wave that rubber-bands to 1100px give near-constant pressure with no situational lulls; he may call the cadence flat even if the run feels intense.
No auto-scroll idle time (v5: 48s idle); the wave and faster chasers keep him moving.

The lane is taller than the view, so walls and B's fast cross-streams can enter from off-screen; a 'came out of nowhere' rock or wall hit is the likeliest cheap-death complaint. The wave warning should read fine.
21.6k px of course at his pace is 2-3 minutes; he won't call it too short.
Walls, rocks and the wave kill both sides; he asked for exactly this and is unlikely to object.

biggestRisk: Pursuers faster than him, spawning continuously from behind, with the wave at his back: the flight becomes 'just keep going right' at flat maximum pressure while the rocks and walls do the killing out of his sight. He can't turn and set a trap without the wave or the next chaser punishing him, so kills feel accidental (P1) and the cadence flat (P2), echoing run 10. Expect him to evaluate his own fix as solving the gravity problem, then name this as the new problem and propose a tweak (chaser waves with gaps, slower or fewer chasers, or a reason to turn back).
abVerdict: Prefers B (~60%), expressed in his own words around asteroid motion, not as 'A vs B': fast streams feel like 'flying about like asteroids', drifting rocks read as nearly static, crowded or like an obstacle course again. ~30% he never names the difference and talks about chasers/wave pressure instead; ~10% he prefers A's calmer field because it leaves more room to plan. Moderate chance he suggests a mix (streams in some sectors, drift in others) as a third option.
